content: The botanical name Dicotyledon Magnoliopsida refers to a class of flowering plants. By definition, this class includes the family Magnoliaceae, but its scope can vary depending on the classification system being used, with some systems being more inclusive and others less so. In the Takhtajan and Cronquist systems, the name Magnoliopsida is used to refer to the group commonly known as dicotyledons. Magnoliopsida in the Takhtajan System The Takhtajan system organizes Magnoliopsida with the following internal taxonomy: Class Magnoliopsida Subclass Magnoliidae Subclass Nymphaeidae Subclass Nelumbonidae Subclass Ranunculidae Subclass Caryophyllidae Subclass Hamamelididae Subclass Dilleniidae Subclass Rosidae Subclass Cornidae Subclass Asteridae Subclass Lamiidae Magnoliopsida in the Cronquist System The Cronquist system, particularly in its 1981 version, uses the following internal taxonomy for Magnoliopsida: Class Magnoliopsida Subclass Magnoliidae Subclass Hamamelidae Subclass Caryophyllidae Subclass Dilleniidae Subclass Rosidae Subclass Asteridae Dahlgren and Thorne Systems The Dahlgren and Thorne systems (1992) also use the name Magnoliopsida to refer to flowering plants, or angiosperms. However, the Cronquist system has been particularly popular, and many versions of it have been published. In some of these Cronquist-based systems, the name Magnoliopsida at the class rank refers to flowering plants (angiosperms) as a whole: Class Magnoliopsida Subclass Magnoliidae Subclass Liliidae Reveal System The Reveal system uses the name Magnoliopsida to refer to a group of primitive dicotyledons, which corresponds to approximately half of the plants within the magnoliids. Its taxonomy is as follows: Class 1. Magnoliopsida Superorder 1. Magnolianae Superorder 2. Lauranae APG Systems In the APG (Angiosperm Phylogeny Group) and APG II systems, botanical names are only used at the rank of order and below. Above the rank of order, these systems use their own names, such as angiosperms, eudicots, monocots, rosids, etc. These names refer to clades, which are unranked. The class Magnoliopsida is not defined in these systems. Furthermore, the APG explicitly rejects the idea that dicotyledons could be a formal taxonomic unit with a formal name, as dicots are considered paraphyletic.
